headline: Software Surges as Jobs Data Rattles Rates; Snowflake Leads the Charge
body_html:
Friday's session is shaping up as a tale of two markets. With 344 names advancing against 197 declining across the 545-stock universe, the tape leans constructive at midday, but the gains are narrow and concentrated. Software is the clear sector leader, up 1.58%, while Industrials add a steady 1.03% and Homebuilders tack on 0.59%. Semiconductors are barely positive at 0.22%. On the other side, Materials are off 0.60%, Energy retreats 0.57%, and Healthcare slips 0.14%.

The standout mover is Snowflake, surging 16.55% and pulling the data-infrastructure complex higher. Twilio and CrowdStrike each add better than 5%, reinforcing the software bid. The macro backdrop, however, offers a complicating wrinkle: the two-year Treasury yield has climbed to its highest level since January 2025 after a stronger-than-expected jobs report revived speculation that the Federal Reserve could resume rate increases — a development that may yet cap equity enthusiasm as the afternoon unfolds.

Geopolitical tension is the day's other dominant undercurrent. Diesel prices hit a record as refinery disruptions tied to the Ukraine and Iran conflicts stoke inflation concerns, pressuring Energy and Materials while keeping the broader reflation trade on edge. Victoria's Secret and Ciena headline the decliners, dropping 13.17% and 10.36% respectively. Watch whether the rate-sensitivity of the Software rally holds as the yield move deepens into the close.

briefs.headline: Hot Jobs Print Sends Short-End Yields to 19-Month High
briefs.body: A stronger-than-forecast employment report is reshaping rate expectations mid-session, pushing the two-year Treasury yield to territory not seen since January 2025. Traders are now pricing a non-trivial probability that the Federal Reserve could lift rates again, adding a hawkish undertone that may test equity valuations as the afternoon progresses.

briefs.headline: Snowflake Rockets 16.5%, Anchors a Broad Software Rally
briefs.body: Snowflake is Friday's runaway leader, surging 16.55% and lifting sentiment across the data and cloud infrastructure space. Twilio gained 6.06% and CrowdStrike added 5.68%, suggesting investors are rotating toward high-growth software names despite the rising-rate backdrop. The Software sector as a whole leads all groups, up 1.58% at midday.

briefs.headline: Record Diesel Prices Fan Inflation Fears Amid Mideast Conflict
briefs.body: Diesel has reached an all-time high as fighting involving Ukraine and Iran disrupts refinery output across two continents simultaneously. The development is amplifying existing inflation concerns and weighing on Energy and Materials sectors, both of which are among the session's laggards. Tidewater and Alpha Metallurgical Resources are each off roughly 6–7%.

briefs.headline: Victoria's Secret Tumbles More Than 13% to Lead Decliners
briefs.body: Consumer-apparel name Victoria's Secret is the session's worst performer, shedding 13.17% without an obvious single catalyst immediately apparent at midday. The decline drags on the broader Consumer sector, which is clinging to a slim 0.17% gain, suggesting the selling is idiosyncratic rather than sector-wide.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Shipping Volumes Remain Subdued as Geopolitical Risk Lingers
briefs.body: Gulf shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is running below its 10-day average, according to vessel-tracking data, as traders weigh the risk of further disruption from the U.S.-Iran conflict. South Korea confirmed it is reviewing military options for the waterway, though no decision has been made, adding another layer of uncertainty to energy-supply estimates.

briefs.headline: Adobe Names New Chief Executive to Succeed Longtime Leader Narayen
briefs.body: Software giant Adobe has appointed Anil Chakravarthy as its next chief executive, succeeding Shantanu Narayen in a high-profile leadership transition. The announcement is drawing attention across the enterprise-software space at a moment when the sector is already outperforming, though Adobe itself is not among the names in our coverage universe today.
